payload.title: Wedding Veil Meaning and Why Brides Wear One
payload.excerpt: Why brides wear veils, from the flame-coloured Roman veil to Queen Victoria's Honiton lace: the veil in faith traditions, who lifts it, wearing a family veil, and how to wear and carry a veil at a destination wedding.
key_takeaways: Brides wear veils for history, faith and family, and for the moment it is lifted, a custom that reaches back to ancient Rome.
Queen Victoria wore her Honiton lace veil in 1840 thrown back over a wreath of orange blossom, not over her face, in the Victorian way of wearing lace at the back of the head.
At a Jewish wedding, the badeken is its own moment before the chupah, when the groom covers the bride's face with the veil.
In English folklore, a veil borrowed from a happily married bride is counted lucky, which makes a family veil both something borrowed and an heirloom.

faq.q: Why does the veil cover the bride's face?
faq.a: It depends on the tradition. At a Jewish wedding, the groom covers the bride's face at the badeken, and it stays veiled through the chupah, giving her privacy at a holy time. In many other weddings, a blusher is worn forward so it can be lifted during the ceremony. A Victorian Honiton veil of about 1850 was worn at the back of the head instead.

faq.q: Who takes the veil off the bride's face?
faq.a: Usually the partner after the vows, a parent at the top of the aisle, or the bride herself. Couples decide in advance and practise once at the rehearsal.

faq.q: Can I wear my mother's wedding veil?
faq.a: Yes, and a veil borrowed from a happily married bride has long been counted lucky. Have it checked early for cleaning or repair, and agree with your mother how it travels and when it goes home.

faq.q: When do you take the veil off?
faq.a: Many brides wear it for the ceremony and portraits, then take it off for the reception.
It can be. The veil has been part of the Christian wedding since the early Christian centuries, and the badeken is part of a Jewish wedding. Many brides wear one for reasons of family or style.

faq.q: What does a veil symbolise in a wedding?
faq.a: In Jewish tradition, it shows that the groom values the bride's inner beauty, not only her outward beauty. In English folklore, a borrowed veil from a happy bride brings luck.
